Their annual spending is $5,650 × 12 = $67,800. Social Security and the pension provide $36,000 + $21,600 = $57,600, leaving a $10,200 annual shortfall. Ignoring taxes and assuming those income and spending amounts apply throughout 2026, that is the IRA withdrawal needed.
ANSWER: 10200

Annual spending at $101,400 per month is $1,216,800. Their Social Security and pension total $87,000 per year, so the shortfall is $1,129,800. This is the amount needed from the IRA under the stated assumptions; their IRA balance is less than that, so the assets listed would not cover the full-year shortfall.
ANSWER: 1129800

Priya is under 65, so the senior deduction does not apply. Her traditional 401(k) deferral reduces wages to $95,500; subtracting the 2026 single standard deduction of $16,100 gives $79,400 of taxable income. Applying the 2026 single brackets (10% through $12,400, 12% through $50,400, then 22%) gives $1,240 + $4,560 + $6,380 = $12,180.
ANSWER: 12180

Mateo is under 65, so he does not qualify for the senior deduction. His $38,000 traditional 401(k) deferral reduces taxable wages to $105,000; after the $16,100 2026 single standard deduction, taxable income is $88,900. Tax is $1,240 on the first $12,400, $4,560 on the next $38,000, and 22% of the remaining $38,500 ($8,470), totaling $14,270.
ANSWER: 14270

Odette was born in 2011 and will be 14 or 15 during 2026, far below the age when an owner of a traditional IRA generally must begin required minimum distributions. Based on the facts given, her required minimum distribution for 2026 is zero.
ANSWER: 0

Priya turns 77 in 2026. Under the standard Uniform Lifetime Table, the divisor at age 77 is 22.9. Dividing the prior December 31 IRA balance of $785,000 by 22.9 gives approximately $34,279.
ANSWER: 34279

At age 70, Imani is three years past her full retirement age of 67. Delayed retirement credits add 8% for each full year after full retirement age, or 24% total. Ignoring cost-of-living adjustments, $3,950 × 1.24 = $4,898 per month.
ANSWER: 4898

The notes conflict: they say Kofi has had no earned income of any kind since 2021, but also report $87,000 of W-2 wages for 2026, which ordinarily represents earned income. I need clarification whether those wages are truly his 2026 wages or whether the employment/no-earned-income description is correct before I can calculate tax reliably.
ANSWER: NEED_INFO

Ivo is 43, so the senior deduction does not apply. His $20,000 traditional 401(k) deferral reduces wages to $138,000; after the $16,100 single standard deduction, taxable income is $121,900. Applying the 2026 brackets yields $1,240 + $4,560 + 22% of $55,300 ($12,166), for total federal income tax of $17,966.
ANSWER: 17966

Mateo is over 65. Based on the 2026 rules, 85% of his $22,200 Social Security benefit is taxable because his provisional income exceeds the threshold; that is $18,870. Adding his $34,560 taxable pension gives $53,430 of income. After the $16,100 standard deduction, the $2,050 age-based additional standard deduction, and the $6,000 senior deduction, taxable income is $29,280. Tax at the 10% and 12% brackets is $3,266 rounded.
ANSWER: 3266
